title: Choose Open Dialer v2's working world
question: The app needs a working visual system. Keep the assigned route-board direction, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Route board
options.thesis: A calm route board that puts the next responsible call at the top of the schedule.
options.viewport: A familiar product shell leads with a call queue, due time, compliance state, and one clear next action.
options.risk: Can feel transport-themed if the route rhythm overwhelms ordinary product controls.

raised.raise: A named information-density discipline keeps dates, counts, and outcomes scanable without visual noise.
One-pixel rules and an annotation rail make compliance context precise at every size.

options.label: Studio ledger
options.lineage: editorial production notes and proof sheets
options.thesis: Each lead reads as a working record with its promise, history, and next edit visible together.
options.viewport: A standard app shell surrounds a lead queue with a focused contact dossier and a durable follow-up rail.
options.risk: More familiar than the route-board system, so it may be less memorable.

options.label: Reference setting
options.thesis: Calls and compliance notes move beside the lead list as a compact apparatus.
options.viewport: A conventional product layout pairs the calling queue with a narrow, keyed compliance rail.
options.case: Strong on precision and auditability, but the dense reading posture slows an operator who is moving through calls.
options.risk: Can make a rapid work queue feel overly academic.

options.label: Data field
options.thesis: A monochrome field turns calling activity into signal and cadence.
options.viewport: A product shell uses dense call metrics above an ordinary lead queue.
options.risk: Pure contrast and motion obscure the human decision at the center of every call.
options.kept: Information density with explicit, easily scanned numeric rhythm.

options.label: Timetable rack
options.thesis: The day is a sequence of scheduled outcomes on a raked information rail.
options.viewport: A familiar workspace uses scheduling rhythm to frame the upcoming calls and follow-ups.
options.risk: The directional metaphor is too close to the product's queue mechanics and could become a costume.
options.kept: A clear chronology that exposes the next commitment without turning controls into decoration.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean sales dashboard with conventional navigation, tables, and forms.
canonCard.viewport: The expected call dashboard, executed cleanly and predictably.
canonCard.risk: It offers little evidence that this tool takes careful calling seriously.
